warnings: The EU-ready source inventory input (source_inventory_eu_ready.jsonl) was a reproducible, derived filter of the canonical sources/source_inventory.jsonl (rows with eu_readiness=ready) and was removed as an execution intermediate at stage finalization per docs/run-artifact-contract.md; this input entry is marked required=false (not required to persist on disk) so the run-contract check does not misread a correctly cleaned-up intermediate as a missing required artifact. It was regenerable from source_inventory.jsonl at any time.

Extraction was distributed across 14 parallel extraction passes (9 dedicated to the largest single documents, 5 covering batches of smaller/medium sources) to cover all 50 EU-ready sources within this session; all fragment outputs were structurally validated (required fields, allowed engineering_dimension/confidence enums, evidence_quote<=320 chars, no disallowed fields, source_id resolves to an EU-ready source) before being merged into the canonical evidence_units.jsonl. Two evidence_quote values were found 1-4 characters over the 320-char schema limit during pre-merge validation and were trimmed to genuine, shorter verbatim substrings of the same source passage before merging (OFF-003 EU-21, OFF-010 EU-01).

3 of the 50 EU-ready sources yielded zero Evidence Units after review: OFF-033 and OFF-034 (Federal Register notices whose preserved text is a very short access page with no substantive rule text beyond the notice header) and RES-023 (a repository landing page for the Colorado River Basin Study with no report body text available). This is a legitimate content-quality outcome, not an extraction gap; these sources remain in source_inventory_eu_ready.jsonl for traceability with no corresponding EUs.

For 9 very large documents (250K-2M extracted characters: OFF-007, OFF-005, OFF-003, OFF-010, RES-018, OFF-011, OFF-006, RES-024, OFF-012), extraction used structured sampling (introduction/summary plus spaced windows through the remainder) rather than exhaustive character-by-character reading; this is representative, not exhaustive, coverage of those mega-documents and is noted in the affected EUs' notes fields where applicable.

Coverage is uneven by design: official operating plans, RODs, and technical/model documentation (priority sources per the extraction protocol) received denser extraction (10-22 EUs) than short agency webpages or news items (1-5 EUs).
